title: Day-trader mode: expose generically-computed signals via the stocks/watchlist/portfolio API
description:
Fourth of four dependent follow-up tasks splitting docs/tasks/backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode.json's original checklist item 6 out of that task (see its `decisions` entry for the full split rationale). By the time this task starts, `GET`/`PUT /api/settings/trading-mode` already exists (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode) and `app.signals.engine`/`app.signals.triple_screen` can already generically evaluate whichever `TimeframeTriple` is active (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine) -- this task is purely about the API surface: what `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis`, `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators`, `GET /api/watchlist`, and `GET /api/portfolio`/`GET /api/portfolio/risk` actually report while day-trader mode is active.

Key decision to make and record: whether the existing `weekly_macd_histogram_slope`/`screens.tide`/etc. field names (which read as literally 'weekly' today, see `docs/architecture/API.md`) get renamed to generic long-term/intermediate/short-term names (a breaking API change, needs frontend coordination) or stay as-is and are simply reinterpreted as 'whichever timeframe currently fills that role' while day-trader mode is active (non-breaking, but arguably misleading field naming while day-trader mode is on) -- docs/tasks/backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode.json's own original checklist item 6 explicitly flagged this as an open call, not a settled one. Regenerate `backend/openapi.json` + `frontend/src/api/types.ts` (`python scripts/export_openapi.py` from `backend/`, then `yarn generate:api-types` from `frontend/`) as part of whichever choice is made, per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard.

checklist.step: Decide and record (via `decisions`) the field-naming question above.

Update `app/api/schemas.py`/the relevant routers so `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis`, `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators`, `GET /api/watchlist`, and `GET /api/portfolio`/`GET /api/portfolio/risk` all correctly reflect the active trading mode's generic signal computation.
Regenerate `backend/openapi.json` and `frontend/src/api/types.ts`; keep every documented error case current (per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard).
Unit/integration tests for the updated endpoints under both swing and day-trader mode.

decisions.decision: Existing field names (`screens.tide.trend`, `weekly_macd_histogram_slope`, `screens.wave`/`screens.trigger`, etc.) are NOT renamed to generic long-term/intermediate/short-term equivalents. They stay exactly as-is and are reinterpreted as 'whichever timeframe currently fills that role' while day-trader mode is active. A new `trading_mode: TradingModeOut` field is added to `AnalysisResponse`/`WatchlistResponse` instead, so a client can tell which mode produced the response without needing a field rename to convey it.
decisions.rationale: This app's swing-mode frontend is a real, live consumer today -- every existing page reading `AnalysisResponse.screens.tide.trend`/`.wave`/`.trigger` or `WatchlistItemOut.signal` would need updating for a rename, for a feature (day-trader mode) that has no settings UI yet to even switch into it (frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings is a separate, not-yet-started task) -- there is no way to actually reach day-trader mode as an end user today except a raw `PUT /api/settings/trading-mode` call. Paying a real, immediate breaking-change cost against the app's only production mode, for a mode nothing can currently switch into through the UI, was judged not worth it. The counter-argument (a field literally named `weekly_macd_histogram_slope` that means something other than 'weekly' while day-trader mode is active is genuinely misleading, and a rename now is cheaper than a rename after more code has grown to depend on the old names) is real and was weighed seriously -- but 'weekly_macd_histogram_slope' is one field among many equally mode-relabeled ones (`screens.tide` itself, the whole `WaveScreen`/`TriggerScreen` shape), so a partial rename would be inconsistent and a full rename is the large, coordinated, frontend-touching change this decision is declining to force through un-asked. The new `trading_mode` field resolves the 'genuinely misleading' half of the concern directly: a client (or a person reading a raw response) can always tell which mode produced a given `AnalysisResponse`/`WatchlistResponse`, so the existing field names' literal wording is no longer the only source of truth about what they mean right now. Revisiting the rename is explicitly left open for `frontend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-settings` (or a later task) once day-trader mode has a real UI entry point and this tradeoff's premise (a rename affects nothing reachable in production) no longer holds.

decisions.decision: This PR wires only `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis` and `GET /api/watchlist` (+`GET /api/watchlist/breadth`, which reuses the same `_tide_trend`/`_compute_signal` helpers) into day-trader-mode signal computation. `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators` and `GET /api/portfolio`/`GET /api/portfolio/risk` are deferred to a new follow-up task, `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups` (`depends_on` this task, plus the two sibling tasks below it structurally depends on).
decisions.rationale: `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators` is structurally blocked, not just deprioritized: it's powered by `app.signals.engine.analyse_history()`'s walk-forward per-bar replay, which docs/architecture/Backend.md §10's own 'Not yet landed' list already documents as having no day-trader-mode support -- `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history` (a separate, already-filed, not-yet-started task) is what has to land first. `GET /api/portfolio/risk`'s `protective_stop`/`profit_target`/exit-flag fields are equally blocked: `app.portfolio.risk`/`app.portfolio.profit_target`/`app.portfolio.exits` still unconditionally hard-code swing mode's weekly/daily split today (confirmed via docs/architecture/Backend.md §10 and `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-portfolio-risk`, another already-filed, not-yet-started task covering exactly this). `GET /api/portfolio`'s own per-position `signal`/`confidence`/`confidence_band` fields are NOT structurally blocked the same way (they only need `analyse_day_trader`, already built) -- but wiring only that endpoint's signal field while `GET /api/portfolio/risk` for the same position stays swing-only would leave the two portfolio endpoints inconsistently day-trader-aware, and `GET /api/portfolio`'s per-position IBKR fetch (one round-trip per held position per request, unlike `GET /api/watchlist`'s already-established per-item pattern) raises its own latency question worth a dedicated design pass rather than a naive sequential loop -- both judged better decided together with the risk-layer work in the follow-up task than rushed in here. This matches this task's own explicit permission to scope down given the endpoint count and swing-mode regression risk, and mirrors `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`'s identical precedent of deferring `app.portfolio.risk`/`profit_target`/`exits` out of its own PR for the same reason.

comments.summary: Blocking: TestDayTraderMode.test_fully_intraday_triple_with_all_legs_available_computes_a_real_signal doesn't discriminate real day-trader-mode computation from a silent fallback to swing-mode data -- the daily/weekly _StubProvider fixture it pairs with the real IBKR fixtures (_buy_daily_ohlcv()/_buy_weekly_ohlcv()) independently produces the exact same signal==BUY/trigger.fired==True/tide==BULLISH assertions under ordinary swing analyse() too. Confirmed via mutation testing (temporarily forcing get_analysis's day-trader branch to False and reverting -- working tree left clean): across the full 1341-test suite only the five explicit 'unavailable' TestDayTraderMode tests failed; this happy-path test and test_swing_mode_default_is_unaffected_by_a_configured_day_trader_triple both kept passing. Same class of gap pr-decision flagged in PR #312. Contrast with test_watchlist.py's own day-trader happy-path test, which correctly discriminates (pairs the day-trader BUY fixture with _StubProvider()'s default HOLD-shaped swing fixture) and does fail under the identical mutation.

Non-blocking (filed on backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups): GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis fetches daily_ohlcv/weekly_ohlcv/extended_data from the swing DataProvider (and maps 404/422/503 from that fetch) before checking whether day-trader mode is active, so a ticker IBKR could fully compute a day-trader signal for, but that the swing provider doesn't recognize or has <26 weeks of weekly history for, gets a 404/422 and never reaches compute_day_trader_signal. GET /api/watchlist's day-trader branch has no such dependency, so the same ticker+mode combination is handled inconsistently between the two endpoints this PR wires up.

review.notes: Independently re-ran backend/frontend tests+coverage (1341/882 passed, 100%/99%+ coverage), static analysis (ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc/profit-target-wording, all clean), regenerated openapi.json/types.ts and diffed clean, did a byte-for-byte swing-mode regression check via real HTTP TestClient calls on main vs this branch (identical aside from the additive trading_mode field), a Playwright browser walkthrough (golden path + day-trader-503 + null-signal edge cases, no console/network errors), and the full persisted e2e suite (26/26 specs pass). Mixed-triple handling, 503-vs-null split, API doc standard, architecture placement of app/api/day_trader_signal.py, and the indicators/portfolio scope-deferral (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups) all checked sound. One blocking finding (non-discriminating happy-path test) sends this back for a fix; one non-blocking finding filed as a followups checklist item. Posted as a COMMENTED-type PR review, not a formal approve/request-changes.
